title: One semax_body lemma per malloc function, assembled by mkVSU into MF_R_VSU
intent: Reduce the correctness proof of the malloc/free Verified Software Unit (VSU) to one self-contained semax_body lemma per function of malloc.prog plus one initializer lemma: mkVSU generates an obligation per function, and each is discharged by exactly one named body lemma (body_X), so the glue is one line per callee.

applicability.goal_shape: A VSU (or program-correctness) theorem `@VSU Espec nil imports ltac:(QPprog prog) exports invariant` whose proof is a single `mkVSU prog internal_specs` invocation followed by one obligation per function of `prog`: a `semax_body Vprog Gprog f_X X_spec` goal for each internal function plus a `VSU_initializer` goal for the global invariant.
applicability.use_when: the program is a fixed set of C functions each with its own funspec; each function's body can be verified in isolation as a self-contained `semax_body` lemma named `body_X`; the bodies communicate only through `forward_call` on their specs; and the initial invariant can be established by one separate lemma (`create_memmgr_R` here).
applicability.avoid_when: a function's correctness depends on a whole-program invariant that cannot be threaded through its funspec (here `mem_mgr_R` is threaded through every spec so each body stays independent); the bodies are too interdependent to verify in isolation; or a body cannot be closed at all (VSU_mmap0.v leaves `body_mmap0`/`body_munmap` as `Parameter`, so that unit's mkVSU defers rather than proves).

claims.claim: The parent MF_R_VSU is closed by a single `mkVSU malloc.prog MF_internal_specs` invocation plus 13 one-line discharges — 12 `solve_SF_internal body_X` (one per internal function) and one `apply create_memmgr_R` for the initializer — across VSU_malloc.v lines 45-58, with nothing else between `Proof.` and `Qed.`.

No `admit`, `Admitted`, `sorry`, `Axiom` or `Parameter` appears in VSU_malloc.v or any of the ten `verif_*.v` files that hold the body lemmas, so every function's body is closed by a real proof (protocol section 4, E3).
claims.evidence: grep -nE '\b(admit|Admitted|sorry|Axiom|Parameter)\b' over the 11 copied files VSU_malloc.v and verif_*.v returned no matches

claims.claim: Measured from the copied files: direct_lemmas = 13 (the 12 body lemmas plus create_memmgr_R, the 13 names discharged at VSU_malloc.v:46-58), glue_lines = 16 (VSU_malloc.v:44-59, the Proof..Qed block), child_lines = [4, 83, 32, 3, 13, 13, 49] (the seven shown children's Lemma..Qed ranges), and depth = 3 along the chain MF_R_VSU -> body_list_from_block -> list_from_inv_remainder -> list_from_inv_remainder'.
claims.evidence: depth chain: VSU_malloc.v:52 (solve_SF_internal body_list_from_block), verif_list_from_block.v:291 (apply (list_from_inv_remainder ...)), verif_list_from_block.v:82 (erewrite list_from_inv_remainder')

claims.claim: All 12 body lemmas share the same per-callee signature — each is `Lemma body_X : semax_body MF_Vprog MF_Gprog f_X X_spec` naming exactly one function and one funspec — so the glue `solve_SF_internal body_X` needs no per-function argument beyond the lemma name.
claims.evidence: read of the ten verif_*.v files; e.g. verif_bin2size2bin.v:7 (body_bin2size, f_bin2size/bin2size_spec), verif_malloc_free.v:8 and :41 (body_malloc/body_free, malloc_spec_R'/free_spec_R'), verif_malloc_large.v:10 (body_malloc_large, malloc_large_spec)

claims.claim: The same `mkVSU` + `solve_SF_internal` per-function pattern appears in the sibling unit MM0_VSU (VSU_mmap0.v:46-60), discharged one per function by `solve_SF_external body_munmap`, `solve_SF_internal body_mmap0`, `solve_SF_internal body_placeholder`; there `body_mmap0`/`body_munmap` are left as `Parameter` (unproved), whereas malloc's 12 bodies are all real lemmas.

metrics.how_counted: parent_lines = VSU_malloc.v lines 40-59 (Definition MF_R_VSU through Qed.); glue_applications = 12 `solve_SF_internal body_X` + 1 `apply create_memmgr_R` across lines 46-58; body_lemmas = the 12 `Lemma body_* : semax_body ...` declarations in the ten verif_*.v files; initializer_lemmas = create_memmgr_R in VSU_malloc.v:20-23

consequences: mkVSU creates one obligation per function of malloc.prog (12 semax_body goals plus one VSU_initializer goal), each of which must be closed by a named body lemma; a single unproved body fails the whole VSU. The move pays off when the bodies are independent: the API functions malloc/free/pre_fill/try_pre_fill carry an index i so one body lemma proves the spec family (malloc_spec_R' R_APD i, free_spec_R' R_APD i, ...) for every i, and the private specs thread the shared invariant mem_mgr_R so no body needs a global argument. Failure modes: a body that cannot be closed must be deferred (as VSU_mmap0.v defers body_mmap0/body_munmap by declaring them Parameter), and a spec that is too weak or too strong at one function surfaces only as an entailment failure deep inside that one body's proof.
